context: Hiroshi (the boss) has unexpectedly come to visit Hiroshi (his father, the retired professor) on a weeknight. The father pours tea slowly.
purpose: father-son evening visit — composed son slowly admitting tiredness

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 父さん、夜分にすまない。
lines.en: Dad — sorry for calling so late.
lines.style: Quiet, composed apology at the threshold. Voice steady but carrying the weight of the visit. A man asking permission to unburden.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いえ、いつでも。お茶でも飲んでいきなさい。
lines.en: No — anytime. Come in. Have some tea.
lines.style: Slow, unhurried welcome. The voice of someone who has been waiting for this. Sets cup down without ceremony.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.style: A full release held in one breath. The body lets go before words can. Tie loosens in the silence.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 仕事、今日も長かったか。
lines.style: Small, careful question. Voice pitched low, almost conspiratorial. The kind of asking that says: I'm listening, take your time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: まあな。…本当に、最近、何も考えられない。
lines.en: Yeah. …Honestly, I can't seem to think about anything anymore.
lines.style: Unguarded admission under controlled breath. Voice tires on the confession. A rare crack in the composed exterior.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。…そういう時期、誰にもある。
lines.en: Mm. …Everyone has a phase like that.
lines.style: Grounded normalization delivered with full presence. No rush. The voice anchors the moment without minimizing it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 父さんは、どう乗り越えた？
lines.en: Dad — how did you get through it?
lines.style: Rare directness from him. The question comes from genuine need, not performance. Voice slightly lower, asking as a person, not as a manager.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: …(pause) 少し、立ち止まる。本当に、少しだけ。
lines.en: …(pause) You stop a little. Really — just a little.
lines.style: Considered answer after real silence. Slow, measured delivery. Each word weighted. The voice of someone who has lived this answer.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.style: Small repetition — he's tasting the word, testing its shape. Voice turns inward. Not skeptical, but wondering if it's possible.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 今、一週間でも、お茶飲んで、本読んで。
lines.en: Even a week right now. Drink tea, read books. Nothing else.
lines.style: Practical wisdom delivered simply. Voice carries gentle firmness — not a suggestion, but a gift offered with steady conviction.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 一週間、本当に取れるかな…
lines.en: A whole week — I don't know if I can actually take that.
lines.style: Doubtful half-laugh, genuine and unforced. The practicality wars with the longing. Voice catches slightly on the doubt.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 取りなさい。時間は、本当に、大切。
lines.en: Take it. Time really does matter.
lines.style: Firm-soft directive with the weight of lived experience behind it. Voice steady, patient, unshakeable. Not negotiable, but said with love.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: …(small breath) ありがとう、父さん。
lines.style: Gratitude catches in the throat. Small breath before speaking. Voice softens completely — the vulnerability of real thanks.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: もう一杯、飲んでいきなさい。
lines.en: Have another cup before you go.
lines.style: Closing gesture without closure. Voice warm, practical. Pours again — the conversation continues in the silence of tea.
